## Summary

F002 (command inventory population) was substantially landed by the earlier "inventory prep" commit, so I verified it against all five acceptance criteria rather than rebuilding it. The `command_guidance.py` module populates a `CommandGuidance` entry for every one of the 32 current top-level commands by projecting `command_validation.known_subcommands()` (exact parity, no extras or gaps), and each entry carries a class, audience, examples, predecessor hints, and a human-escalation rule that round-trip through the F001 model — with all six workflow groups (readonly_inspection, lifecycle_mutation, dispatch_paid_work, configuration_mutation, diagnostic_inspection, human_handoff) represented and zero command-execution paths in the module. To close the gap between the prep work and F002's full acceptance, I added two regression tests: one asserting the *populated* inventory covers all six command classes (criterion 3, beyond merely the enum being closed), and one asserting *every* entry — not just the representative sample — carries complete metadata that validates through the F001 model (criterion 2). The targeted test file now passes 20/20; I did not run
